claims.claim: Summary: Corral is the Mexican forward for Pachuca Femenil
claims.note: OneFootball names Pachuca Femenil forward; Concacaf confirms Pachuca career.

claims.claim: Won the women's striker prize at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London
claims.note: beIN: received the Women's Gerd Müller Trophy at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. Concacaf: honored as 2026 Women's Striker of the Year by France Football.

claims.claim: Ceremony held Monday 26 October 2026 in London
claims.note: beIN: Monday, October 26 in London. OneFootball: this Monday, October 26, in London.

claims.claim: Concacaf calls the prize 2026 Women's Striker of the Year and says France Football honoured her with it
claims.note: Page: honored as the 2026 Women's Striker of the Year by France Football.

claims.claim: beIN SPORTS and OneFootball call it the Women's Gerd Müller Trophy, given to the top scorer of the year
claims.note: beIN: trophy introduced in 2025 to recognize outstanding goalscorers. OneFootball names the Gerd Müller Trophy.

claims.claim: First Mexican player to win an award at the Ballon d'Or
claims.note: beIN: first Mexican player to win an award at the event. Concacaf: first Mexican player honored at the event in both men's and women's categories.

claims.claim: Concacaf gives her age as 35
claims.note: Page: 'At 35 years old'.

claims.claim: Concacaf describes her as a key member of the Mexico Women's National Team
claims.note: Page describes her as one of the most important players for Las Tuzas and the Mexican Women's National Team.

claims.claim: Yahoo Sports reports she received the top goalscorer prize alongside Harry Kane
claims.note: Yahoo: 'Top Goalscorer' prize; she received her award alongside Harry Kane.

claims.claim: Yahoo describes her as the first Mexican female footballer to receive an award at the gala
claims.note: Page: first Mexican female footballer to receive an award at the ceremony.

claims.claim: Hooligan Soccer calls her the inaugural winner of the women's category, which debuts in 2026
claims.note: Page: 'since the women's category makes its debut in 2026, she is also its inaugural winner.' Not the award's first winner, and the article does not say so.

claims.claim: OneFootball says she became the second female player to receive the award, after Ewa Pajor was named first winner of the women's award introduced in 2025
claims.note: Page: women's award introduced in 2025 with Ewa Pajor as first winner; Corral became the second female player to receive it.

claims.claim: Concacaf gives 43 goals and 11 assists in 46 matches, in what it calls the regular year, without naming a season
claims.note: Page: 'playing in 46 matches in the regular year, scoring 43 goals' and 'delivering 11 assists'. No season name is given.

claims.claim: OneFootball gives the same figures (43 goals, 11 assists, 46 matches) for the 2025-26 season
claims.note: Page: '43 goals and 11 assists in 46 matches during the 2025–2026 season'.

claims.claim: Yahoo Sports and Hooligan Soccer give 49 goals in 49 matches, with no season named
claims.note: Yahoo: 49 goals in 49 matches. Hooligan: 49 goals in 49 appearances. Neither names a season.

claims.claim: Hooligan Soccer gives 53 goals for club and country, with no season or year named
claims.note: Page: 'a sensational season in which she scored 53 goals for club and country'. The 53 figure is not tied to a named season or year.

claims.claim: beIN SPORTS gives 57 goals in the 2025 calendar year, 50 for Pachuca and seven for Mexico
claims.note: Page: 'During the 2025 calendar year' 57 goals, 50 for Pachuca, seven for Mexico.

claims.claim: OneFootball: 20 goals in 21 matches in the previous Liga MX Femenil tournament, and 24 goals in 17 appearances in the current one
claims.note: Page: 20 goals in 21 matches; 24 goals in 17 appearances.

claims.claim: Concacaf calls her Pachuca Femenil's all-time leading scorer with 172 goals in 190 appearances
claims.note: Page: all-time leading scorer in Pachuca Femenil's history with 172 goals in 190 appearances.

claims.claim: She guided Pachuca to its first league title, the Clausura 2025
claims.note: Page: guided Las Tuzas to their first league title during the Clausura 2025 season.

claims.claim: Fox Sports Mexico describes her as a five-time Liga MX Femenil Golden Boot winner
claims.note: Page: 'la cinco veces Campeona de Goleo de la Liga MX Femenil'.

claims.claim: Concacaf's awards page lists her as a 2024/25 Women's Player of the Year nominee, forward, Mexico, Pachuca
claims.note: Page: Women's Player of the Year nominees, 2024/25; Forward; Mexico, Pachuca.

claims.claim: Built her career in Finland and Spain before joining Pachuca
claims.note: Page: impressive career across Finland and Spain before Pachuca.

claims.claim: At Levante in 2017/18 she scored 24 goals and became the first non-Spanish player to win the Liga F top scorer award
claims.note: Page: 24 goals with Levante in 2017/18; first non-Spanish player to win the Liga F Top Scorer award.

claims.claim: Scored 13 goals for Mexico in the 2025/26 Concacaf W Qualifiers
claims.note: Page: 13 for Mexico in the 2025/26 Concacaf W Qualifiers.

claims.claim: beIN SPORTS counts seven goals for Mexico in the 2025 calendar year
claims.note: Page: seven for the Mexico Women's National Team in the 2025 calendar year.

claims.claim: On 9 October 2026 Corral said she had never been nominated for the Ballon d'Or but believed she could have been on another occasion
claims.note: Page dated 9 October 2026: 'en mi caso nunca he estado nominada' and 'hubiera podido también estarlo en otra ocasión'.

claims.claim: Asked about Scarlett Camberos's nomination, she called it something very positive
claims.note: Page: 'es algo muy positivo'. The removed phrase about Mexican football is not used.

valueNote: Sets out the conflicting goal totals and the disputed women's-record claims with their sources, which the top results do not do.
summary: All checked claims match the fetched sources. The season label is attributed only to OneFootball, the Hooligan first-winner wording is corrected, the 53-goal figure is no longer tied to a season, and the Camberos quote is limited to what the source confirms.
